title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 68-70). E is a set with a family Σ_E of 'supports' (admissible subsets). Σ_E is a complete lattice for 'Sup' (not necessarily union). supp°_E(A) is the support generated by an arbitrary subset A. Every S in Σ_E is the Sup of the point-supports S_x, x∈S. The notation |o| means 'disjoint' (no common point / orthogonal) and is used between points, sets and supports. Σ^*_A, Σ^*_A' seem to denote these lattices for the structured objects (E,Σ_E), (E',Σ_E'); the subscript was apparently changed from E to A.

Lemma 1 (previous page). A set map α: E → Σ_E' (or E → P(E')) extends uniquely to a Sup-preserving map α_*: Σ_E → Σ_E', namely α_*(S) = supp°_E'(ᾱ(S)) with ᾱ(S) = ∪_{x∈S} α(x). This gives Hom_Ens(E, Σ_E') ≅ Hom^!_ord(Σ_E, Σ_E'), where ! means maps commuting with arbitrary Sups. This is the free-sup-lattice / 'extension by joins' universal property.

Motivation. Grothendieck wants a notion of transpose for such 'correspondences' that generalizes the case of 'trivial disjunctors' (Σ = all subsets). In that case the transpose of a relation α: E → P(E') is the converse relation: x' ∈ α(x) ⇔ x ∈ β(x'). Equivalently, by negation, x' |o| α(x) ⇔ x |o| β(x').

Lemma 2 (this page). Let α_* be associated with α: E → P(E') as above. The following conditions are claimed to be equivalent:
(i) There is a Sup-preserving β_*: Σ_A' → Σ_A with α_*(S) |o| S' ⇔ S |o| β_*(S') for all supports S, S'. This is an 'adjunction relative to the orthogonality relation'.
(ii) There is a point-level β: E' → P(E) with α(x) |o| x' ⇔ x |o| β(x').
Moreover β_* is unique, and when β is as in (ii), β_* is associated with β: β_*(S') = supp°_E(β̄(S')).
(iii) For every x' in E', put β̄(x') = {x ∈ E | α(x) |o| x'}; one wants this set (or, per the next page, its complement) to be a support in Σ_E.
A marginal (iv) proposes: for each S in Σ_E', {x | ᾱ(x) ⊂ S} ∈ Σ_E, a continuity-type preimage condition. It also queries whether α_*(supp°(A)) = supp°(ᾱ(A)) holds for arbitrary A.

Next page. β_*(x') = complement of β̄(x') (a 'cosupport'). Maps satisfying these conditions are named 'correspondances disjonctives'. The 'scholie' says transposition t is an involutive bijection Corrdis(E,E') ↔ Corrdis(E',E).

In modern terms: for an orthogonality relation ⊥ on complete lattices, a join-preserving f has a ⊥-transpose g with f(a) ⊥ b ⇔ a ⊥ g(b). Via S ↦ S^⊥ this is the existence of a right adjoint composed with polarities. At point level this is exactly the Chu-space morphism (adjointness) condition r'(f x, x') = r(x, g x'), with r = the non-disjointness relation. Equivalently, it is a 'bond'/Galois-adjoint relation in formal concept analysis. The criterion (iii)/(iv) is the closedness condition guaranteeing that such an adjoint exists.
errors: Condition (iii) as written ('On veut β̄(x') ∈ Σ_E', with β̄(x') = {x | α(x) |o| x'}) seems inconsistent with the next page. There β_*(x') = C(β̄(x')), the complement, is identified as a cosupport. So the correct requirement is presumably on the complement, or Σ_E should be read as 'open'/co-closed sets. The page leaves this unsettled.
Uniqueness of β_* in (i) needs the orthogonality to be separating: a support must be determined by the set of supports disjoint from it. This hypothesis is not stated on this page.

The equivalence (i)⇔(ii)⇔(iii) is stated, not proved. The listing is tentative ('?' in the condition list, a marginal (iv) still being formulated). The marginal also flags that α_*(supp°A) = supp°(ᾱ(A)) is not clear for non-closed A (cf. the previous page's margin).
Writing (ii) as β: E' → P(E) while (i) lives in Σ suggests the point/support passage is not yet fixed; x |o| β(x') must be interpreted via point-supports S_x.

ideas.what: Unique extension of a point map E → Σ_E' to a Sup-preserving map Σ_E → Σ_E' (Lemma 1, previous page)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard lattice theory (e.g. Joyal–Tierney 1984 for Sup; folklore earlier)

ideas.what: Transpose of a join-preserving correspondence relative to a disjointness relation: α_*(S) |o| S' ⇔ S |o| β_*(S'), and its point-level form α(x) |o| x' ⇔ x |o| β(x')
ideas.modern_name: Chu-space morphism / adjoint pair relative to an orthogonality (polarity); 'bonds' in formal concept analysis; Galois-connection duality of sup-lattices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Barr (Chu construction, 1979), Pratt (Chu spaces, 1990s); Wille/Ganter (FCA, 1980s); Birkhoff/Ore (Galois connections)

ideas.what: Criterion for existence of the transpose: the 'preimage' set {x | α(x) |o| x'} (or {x | ᾱ(x) ⊂ S}) must be a support/cosupport
ideas.modern_name: Continuity-type condition for existence of adjoints between closure systems (analogue of continuity of relations / lower-upper semicontinuity of multifunctions)

ideas.what: Involutive transposition on 'disjunctive correspondences' Corrdis(E,E') ≅ Corrdis(E',E), generalizing converse relations ('trivial disjunctors')
ideas.modern_name: Self-duality of the category of Chu spaces / of relations (dagger structure)

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck independently sets up a framework of 'disjunctors' with orthogonality-adjoint 'disjunctive correspondences' and an involutive transpose. This is essentially Chu-space / formal-concept-analysis duality, arrived at from his own 'ateliers' project, and is not cited in that literature. The novelty is historical rather than mathematical.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's late interest in order-theoretic/logical dualities (orthogonality, disjunction). This could inform how his 1986 'ateliers'/'disjoncteurs' material relates to Chu spaces and linear-logic-style dualities. However, the mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but elementary order-theoretic lemma: existence and uniqueness of a transpose with respect to a disjointness relation, i.e. a Chu/Galois-type adjunction. It is historically interesting as part of an unpublished 1986 'disjoncteurs' framework, but contains no result a specialist would find new.
